models_evaluated: neural network model predicting in-hospital death and ICU admission

links.outcome: ML model vs clinician predictions of ICU admission or death on the same hospitalizations
links.effect: ML median F1 0.32, AUC 0.77 vs clinicians F1 0.33, AUC 0.64; ML more accurate than clinicians for ICU admission.
links.quote: ML predictions were more accurate than clinicians for ICU admission.

links.outcome: Combined human-plus-model prediction sensitivity versus clinicians alone or model alone
links.effect: Combined predictions detected 49% of deterioration events, improving sensitivity by 16% vs clinicians alone and 24% vs model alone, with PPV of 33%.
links.quote: Combining human and model predictions detected 49% of clinical deterioration events, improving sensitivity by 16% compared with clinicians alone and 24% compared with the model alone while maintaining a positive predictive value of 33%, thus keeping false alarms at a clinically acceptable level.

screen.reason: The study compares model-alone, clinician-alone, and human-AI combination strategies to evaluate the benefit of combining ML predictions with physician/nurse judgment for inpatient deterioration.

primary.practice: combining AI predictions with clinician judgment
